keyTakeaways: 20 DIY Halloween costumes across 6 core materials take 1 to 6 hours and an estimated $5 to $30 each.
17 of the 20 builds need no sewing: hot glue for card and foam, fabric glue for felt, a needle only for parts that carry weight.
A homemade costume has no flame-resistance label; CPSC advice is to avoid flimsy materials and billowing sleeves, add reflective tape and keep eyeholes large enough for full vision.

In a 2026 study of 11,144 Americans' time use, participatory arts including crafts showed moderate happiness and the highest average stress and sadness of eight activities: making is rewarding, not restful.

faqs.question: How do I make a Halloween costume without sewing?
faqs.answer: Use hot glue for cardboard, foam and props, and fabric glue for felt on felt. On this list, 17 of the 20 builds need no needle; only the octopus, the headless horseman and the rain cloud's hanging raindrops call for one.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest homemade Halloween costume?
faqs.answer: On our estimates the astronaut jetpack is cheapest at about $5 to $10, because it uses two empty bottles and box card. Any thrift build costs less again if you already own the base garment.

faqs.question: How long does a DIY Halloween costume take to make?
faqs.answer: Between 1 and 6 hours for the builds here: the fortune teller takes about 1 hour and the EVA leaf armor about 6. Add drying time for paint and fabric glue, so start a skill-3 build several days before 31 October.

faqs.question: What glue should I use on felt?
faqs.answer: Fabric glue for felt-on-felt joints that need to bend, and stitches for anything that carries weight. Hot glue is fine for a quick fix but tends to peel off fabric that stretches.

faqs.question: How do I stop a cardboard costume going soggy?
faqs.answer: Brush on PVA glue or primer before painting, which stops paint warping the board. It is still a one-night material, so choose felt or foam if rain is forecast.

faqs.question: Can you paint EVA foam with acrylic?
faqs.answer: Yes, once it is sealed: pass a heat gun over the surface, then add 2 to 3 coats of flexible primer before the acrylic. Keep solvent spray paint off white polystyrene craft foam, which it can dissolve.

faqs.question: Are homemade Halloween costumes a fire risk?
faqs.answer: They can be, because nobody has tested your materials as clothing. The CPSC advises avoiding flimsy materials and big baggy sleeves or billowing skirts, so keep fiberfill, tissue and felt spikes well away from candles.

faqs.question: Is a cardboard box costume safe for kids trick-or-treating?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the child can see sideways and walk freely. The CPSC advises eyeholes big enough for full vision, costumes short enough not to trip on, and reflective tape that shows up in car headlights.

faqs.question: What tools do I need to start making costumes?
faqs.answer: Scissors, a glue gun, a box cutter and fabric glue cover most of the 20 builds here. The three EVA builds add a heat gun, and the butterfly and horseman need pliers to bend wire hangers.

faqs.question: Can I send a photo of my homemade costume as a Halloween card?
faqs.answer: Yes. The SubhSandesh Halloween card holds up to six photos and a letter, and the recipient opens the link in any phone or laptop browser with no app or account. It is made for one person, with partner, bestie, family and kids modes.

faqs.question: Do kids care more about a costume they helped make?
faqs.answer: A 2022 study of 128 children in the UK and India found 5- and 6-year-olds valued a toy they assembled over an identical copy. It studied toys, not costumes, but it suggests a homemade build earns attachment even when it is wonky.

article.contentMarkdown:
# DIY Halloween Costumes: 20 Builds With Materials, Hours and Cost

The best DIY Halloween costumes start from one core material you can work: cardboard, felt, old sheets, paper and paint, EVA foam or thrift finds. Below are 20 builds, each with materials, tools, skill level (1–3), hours, estimated cost and steps.

SubhSandesh builds greeting pages, so our data covers timing and the photo. The closest festival we have measured is Raksha Bandhan, not Halloween, and the sample is small: 49.4% of 89 rakhi pages were built on the day itself, a habit no 6-hour build survives. And 48.3% of views of shared SubhSandesh pages happen on a phone, so each build must read in a small photo.

## What counts as a DIY Halloween costume, and is making one worth it?

A DIY Halloween costume is one you construct rather than assemble: you cut, glue, sew or paint its main element. A closet outfit with a prop is a costume; an arcade cabinet is a build.

Making is not pure relaxation. In [a 2026 analysis of 11,144 American Time Use Survey respondents](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13031343), participatory arts, including crafts, showed moderate happiness and the highest average stress and sadness of eight health-enhancing activities.

The payoff is ownership. In [a 2022 study of 128 children aged 5 to 6 in the UK and India](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8958763), children valued a toy they assembled over an identical copy, with or without a partner's help.

## 20 DIY Halloween costumes, grouped by core material

Skill 1 needs scissors and glue; skill 2 adds cutting, heat-shaping or sewing; skill 3 means a frame or dozens of parts. Costs are our estimates for US craft or thrift supplies.

### 1. Cardboard: 4 builds

Cardboard is cheap, rigid and not weatherproof. Use plain-sided moving boxes.

- **Arcade cabinet** (skill 2, 3h, est. $10–15). Materials: tall box, acrylics, 6 bottle caps, printed game screen. Tools: box cutter, glue gun. Steps: cut an eye-level window; paint; add cap buttons; frame with the print.
- **Knight armor** (skill 2, 4h, est. $12–18). Materials: 2 boxes, silver acrylic, elastic, brass fasteners. Tools: box cutter, glue gun. Steps: cut chest and shoulder plates; score and curve; join; paint.
- **Instant camera** (skill 1, 2h, est. $6–10). Materials: shoebox, paper cup, white card. Tools: scissors, glue gun. Steps: paint the box; glue on the cup lens; cut a slot; feed out a doodled "print".
- **Astronaut jetpack** (skill 1, 2h, est. $5–10). Materials: two 2-liter bottles, card panel, foil tape, orange tissue, old straps. Tools: glue gun. Steps: foil-tape the bottles; glue to the panel; add tissue "flames".

### 2. Felt and fabric: 4 builds

Felt does not fray, so cut edges can stay raw. Three builds start from a plain hoodie.

- **Dragon hoodie** (skill 2, 3h, est. $15–25). Materials: green hoodie, green and yellow felt, fiberfill. Tools: needle or fabric glue. Steps: cut 10 to 12 spike pairs; stuff; sew down hood and spine.
- **Octopus** (skill 2, 3h, est. $15–20). Materials: purple hoodie, 3 pairs of tights, fiberfill, felt circles. Tools: needle and thread. Steps: stuff 6 tight legs; sew around the hem; glue on suckers.
- **Hedgehog** (skill 2, 4h, est. $15–20). Materials: brown hoodie, brown and tan felt. Tools: scissors, fabric glue. Steps: cut zigzag strips; glue overlapping rows from hem to hood; add a nose.
- **Monarch butterfly** (skill 2, 3h, est. $10–15). Materials: 2 wire hangers, orange and black felt, elastic. Tools: pliers, glue gun. Steps: bend wing frames; glue felt over; add veins; loop shoulder elastic.

### 3. Old sheets and clothes: 3 builds

These come out of the linen cupboard. Prefer tightly woven pieces worn close (see safety).

- **Medusa** (skill 1, 1.5h, est. $8–12). Materials: flat sheet, gold cord, headband, 8 to 10 rubber snakes. Tools: glue gun, safety pins. Steps: pin the sheet snug as a toga; belt it; glue snakes to the headband.
- **Headless horseman** (skill 3, 5h, est. $15–25). Materials: long dark coat, wire hanger, card, dark mesh, foam pumpkin. Tools: pliers, glue gun, needle. Steps: build a shoulder frame above your head; button the coat over; sew in a mesh eye window.
- **Rain cloud** (skill 1, 2h, est. $10–15). Materials: old gray T-shirt, fiberfill, blue felt, thread. Tools: glue gun, needle. Steps: glue on fiberfill puffs; cut felt raindrops; hang them from the hem.

### 4. Paper and paint: 3 builds

Paint does the work here, so budget drying time. Use fabric paint on anything that bends.

- **Stained-glass window** (skill 2, 3h, est. $8–12). Materials: black poster board, colored tissue, contact film, ribbon. Tools: craft knife. Steps: cut an arched lattice frame; back with tissue; seal in film; hang on ribbon.
- **Starry Night jacket** (skill 2, 4h, est. $12–20). Materials: denim jacket, blue, yellow and white fabric paint. Tools: brushes, chalk. Steps: chalk the swirls of Van Gogh's 1889 painting; paint dark blues first; add stars; heat-set.
- **Pop-art comic hero** (skill 1, 1.5h, est. $8–12). Materials: red face paint, dot stencil, white card, dowel. Tools: sponge, black marker. Steps: sponge dots on one cheek; outline features; carry a speech bubble.

### 5. Foam and EVA: 3 builds

EVA foam bends with heat and holds shape when cool. Use 2 mm for details, 5 mm for armor.

- **Pharaoh collar and headdress** (skill 2, 3h, est. $15–20). Materials: 2 mm EVA, gold and blue acrylic, striped fabric, elastic. Tools: heat gun, glue gun. Steps: cut a half-moon collar; heat-curve; paint bands; pleat fabric onto elastic.
- **Viking helmet and shield** (skill 2, 4h, est. $15–25). Materials: 5 mm EVA, 2 ft foam circle, silver and brown paint. Tools: craft knife, heat gun. Steps: cut a headband and crossing strips; heat-shape a dome; paint the shield.
- **Forest dryad leaf armor** (skill 3, 6h, est. $20–30). Materials: 2 mm EVA, three green acrylics, tank top. Tools: heat gun, glue gun. Steps: cut 60 to 80 leaves; score and heat-curl; dry-brush; glue in rows.

### 6. Thrift-store remix: 3 builds

Thrift builds start from a garment already the right shape. Buy a size up for warm layers.

- **Zombie prom date** (skill 1, 2h, est. $15–25). Materials: thrift formalwear, cold tea, sandpaper, face paint. Tools: spray bottle. Steps: fray the hems; sand knees and elbows; mist with tea; dry patchy.
- **Fortune teller** (skill 1, 1h, est. $12–20). Materials: 3 thrift scarves, beaded necklaces, frosted plastic ball, tray. Tools: none. Steps: wrap a headscarf; layer a shawl; carry the ball on the tray.
- **Garden gnome** (skill 1, 1.5h, est. $10–18). Materials: oversized cardigan, wide belt, red felt, cotton batting. Tools: glue gun. Steps: roll a felt cone hat; glue a batting beard onto elastic; belt low.

## DIY costume materials compared: hours, cost and durability

The table rolls the 20 builds up by material. Hours, costs and durability are our estimates, not lab tests.

| Material | Skill | Hours | Est. cost | Durability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cardboard | 1–2 | 2–4 | $5–18 | One night; softens in rain |
| Felt and fabric | 2 | 3–4 | $10–25 | Re-wearable; spot-clean |
| Sheets, clothes, thrift | 1–3 | 1–5 | $8–25 | Washable |
| Paper and paint | 1–2 | 1.5–4 | $8–20 | Paper tears; heat-set paint washes |
| EVA foam | 2–3 | 3–6 | $15–30 | Several seasons if sealed |

If rain is forecast for 31 October, choose felt or foam over cardboard. Reused clothing is cheapest, being already paid for.

## Maker basics: glue, cardboard and foam in 3 rules

Three techniques decide whether a build lasts the evening. Each matches the joint to the flex.

### Hot glue vs fabric glue vs sewing

Hot glue grabs in under a minute and suits card, foam and props, but peels off stretchy fabric. Fabric glue stays flexible on felt but often needs hours to cure, so check the bottle. Sew anything carrying weight; a running stitch every 1 cm holds.

### Making cardboard sturdy

Score across the corrugation before bending. Glue flat plates as two layers with corrugations crossed, and prime with PVA so wet paint does not warp them.

### Painting foam

Heat-seal EVA's pores, then apply 2 to 3 coats of flexible primer before acrylic. Keep spray paint off white polystyrene foam, which solvents dissolve.

## Homemade costume safety: what a store label covers and a build does not

The US Consumer Product Safety Commission tells buyers to look for a "Flame Resistant" label on costumes, masks, beards and wigs, noting labelled items can still burn ([CPSC Publication 100, March 2012](https://www.cpsc.gov/s3fs-public/100.pdf)). A homemade build has no label.

- **Flame:** [16 CFR 1610](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-D/part-1610/subpart-A/section-1610.7) classes plain clothing fabric "Rapid and Intense Burning" when test strips average under 3.5 seconds. Fiberfill, tissue and felt spikes were never tested; keep them from candles.
- **Shape:** CPSC warns against flimsy materials and billowing sleeves or skirts, so pin togas snug.
- **Visibility:** reflective tape glows in headlights and is sold in hardware, bicycle and sporting goods stores. Tape dark builds.
- **Vision:** CPSC prefers makeup to masks, with eyeholes large enough for full vision. The [American Academy of Pediatrics](https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/all-around/Pages/Halloween-Safety-Tips.aspx) (updated 29 September 2026) adds: hats must not cover eyes.
- **Props:** swords should be soft and flexible.

## Send the finished build photo as a Halloween card

After 5 hours on a headless horseman, the photo deserves more than a feed post. Our [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) holds up to six photos, so one person sees the build in progress and finished, then reads your letter by flashlight.

It has partner, bestie, family and kids modes, and its Boo License picks from eight classic costumes, not yours, so your photos carry the work. It is a one-person greeting page, not a party invite. If you filmed the build, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes up to 12 photos and a 60-second voice note.

## When to skip DIY, or skip our page

Both lose sometimes. Here are four cases.

- **Under 1 hour left:** only the fortune teller fits.
- **Near a bonfire:** labelled store costumes were flame-tested; these 20 were not.
- **A child out after dark:** face paint beats a frame that blocks side vision.
- **Same room on 31 October:** our pages average 11.1 views because people reopen them remotely; in person, show the photo.

## Sources

- Bone et al., [Experiential wellbeing in time-use data](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13031343), Scientific Reports, 24 February 2026.
- Marsh et al., [The IKEA effect in children](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8958763), Developmental Psychology, April 2022.
- CPSC, [Halloween Safety](https://www.cpsc.gov/s3fs-public/100.pdf), March 2012.
- American Academy of Pediatrics, [Halloween Safety Tips](https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/all-around/Pages/Halloween-Safety-Tips.aspx), updated 29 September 2026.
- eCFR, [16 CFR 1610.7](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-D/part-1610/subpart-A/section-1610.7).
- SubhSandesh data, 24 September 2026; Raksha Bandhan sample, 9 September 2026.
